bc_gold_roche_boulder.blurb: Gold Roche Boulder is a bouldering stop in the Gold Rush cluster of the Fraser Canyon, in British Columbia's Fraser Valley. It is one big golden block that stands right by the road pull-out, so there is no search for it. Five problems cover it, with a back side that carries several of them. The spread runs from V3 up to V7, with a V4 and two V5s in the middle and a single V7 as the top end. A session here pairs easily with the next boulder over, Wu Boulder, since the two sit within a short stroll of each other.

bc_wu_boulder.blurb: Wu Boulder is a second large block in the Gold Rush bouldering cluster of the Fraser Canyon, British Columbia, standing right behind the golden Gold Roche boulder. It has a small cave on one side and a slab face on the opposite side. Five problems share it, and the grades are spread widely: two at V1, one V2, a V4, and one standout V10 for strong climbers. Most of the lines suit someone warming up or working through the easier grades, which makes it a natural second boulder after its neighbour, with the one hard problem as a long-term project.

bc_island_in_the_sky.blurb: Island in the Sky is a small wall within the Smoke Bluffs at Squamish, British Columbia, tucked between The Zip and Car Jack crag a little uphill of the parking lot. It has five routes, four of them trad and one bolted, with grades from 5.7 to 5.10. Two lines sit at 5.8 and two at 5.10, so there is something for a leader stepping up and for a harder warm-down. Crack and corner climbing dominates, including a long corner with a wide twin-crack start. The wall sees fewer parties than the main Bluffs walls, which helps on busy days.

bc_gumby_s_wall.blurb: Gumby's Wall is a small wall in the Smoke Bluffs at Squamish, British Columbia, between Krack Rock and Cabin Boys Office. All five routes are trad, running from 5.8 to 5.10, with three of them in the 5.10 range, and each can be set up as a top rope from above. The face holds shade until close to sunset, so it works when the rest of the Bluffs bakes in summer. After heavy rain it can stay damp for a while, though that rarely matters in the warm months. It suits a day of moderate crack and face climbing.

bc_roadside_distraction.blurb: Roadside Distraction is a small crag in the Smoke Bluffs at Squamish, British Columbia, sitting just above the loop trail between the Mosquito and Neat and Cool areas. It holds five routes: four trad and one sport. The grades start at 5.10 and climb to 5.12, with two at 5.10, two at 5.11 and a single 5.12 bolted line. Several routes begin with awkward undercut moves, so expect the opening moves to be the hard part. This is a spot for climbers already comfortable on 5.10 who want a short, steep detour from the busier walls nearby.

bc_poltergeist.blurb: Poltergeist is a compact cliff of about 35 m in the Browning Bluffs section of Murrin Park near Squamish, British Columbia. Five routes work the face, four bolted and one on gear, and a few share the same starting holds. The grades sit in hard territory: one at 5.11 and four at 5.12, so it is a place for experienced sport climbers rather than a first outing. In summer the wall keeps shade until mid-afternoon, and one dihedral line holds it even longer, which makes it a useful choice on hot days.

bc_south_howser_tower.blurb: South Howser Tower is a high peak in the Howser Towers group of the Bugaboos, in the Purcell Mountains of British Columbia. Its main face rises roughly 2,000 ft and carries only a handful of routes, a mix of long alpine and trad lines with a couple of ice climbs. Rock climbs on it run around 5.10 to 5.11, and the ice goes at WI3 and WI4. Of the three Howser towers it is the easiest to get to, but the day is still a serious alpine undertaking with a glaciated approach, exposure and bergschrunds to deal with.
